steps.intent: Our primary objectives are to unequivocally condemn the 7 October Hamas terrorist attacks, affirm Israel's inherent right of self-defence under Article 51, secure the immediate release of all hostages, and facilitate humanitarian pauses to allow vital aid into Gaza without compromising Israel's security operations. We expect significant opposition and likely vetoes from Russia and China over the explicit affirmation of Israel's right to self-defence and the absence of a call for an immediate, full ceasefire. Additionally, provisions seeking to restrict the flow of weapons and financing to armed groups in Gaza will face pushback from regional and aligned members.

messages.Albania: Albania fully supports the draft resolution presented by the United States. The text accurately reflects our core priorities by unequivocally condemning Hamas's barbaric terrorist attacks of 7 October, demanding the immediate release of hostages, explicitly recognizing the inherent right of self-defence under Article 51, and addressing the urgent humanitarian needs of civilians in Gaza in full respect of international humanitarian law. We stand ready to vote in favour of this text as drafted.
messages.Brazil: Brazil remains committed to Council unity and action to halt the catastrophic humanitarian collapse in Gaza, building on the broad consensus achieved by our compromise draft S/2023/773. To secure our support, this resolution must clearly demand the rescission of the northern Gaza evacuation order rather than appearing to accommodate forced displacement, and it must decisively address the acute fuel and humanitarian supply shortages. The text must remain firmly grounded in international humanitarian law and avoid language that could be construed as authorizing actions that inflict collective punishment on the civilian population.
messages.China: China cannot support the draft resolution in its current form, as it is profoundly unbalanced and evades the most urgent call of the international community and Arab states for an immediate ceasefire. Introducing an unqualified narrative of self-defence while military actions rage only risks giving a green light to further military escalation, widespread civilian casualties, and humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. The Council must act responsibly by demanding an immediate cessation of hostilities, halting collective punishment, and urging the rescission of the evacuation order.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador welcomes the draft resolution presented by the United States, which firmly condemns the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas, demands the immediate release of hostages, and reaffirms the obligation of all parties to strictly adhere to international humanitarian law. To facilitate broader Council consensus and respond to the acute humanitarian emergency on the ground, we encourage explicit reference to the provision of fuel for essential civilian facilities and reinforced safeguards regarding evacuation and civilian displacement. Ecuador remains fully committed to working constructively to ensure the Council takes urgent, decisive action.
messages.France: France welcomes the US initiative and supports the core elements of the draft, notably the unequivocal condemnation of Hamas's heinous terrorist attacks, the recognition of Israel's right to defend itself in accordance with international humanitarian law, and the call for the immediate release of all hostages. To maximize Council unity and respond to the catastrophic situation on the ground, the humanitarian provisions—particularly regarding humanitarian pauses, corridors, and fuel access—must be reinforced. We stand ready to work constructively with the penholder to ensure the swift adoption of this text.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the draft resolution as a vital step to overcome the Council's paralysis and fulfill our mandate to protect civilians and alleviate human suffering. While we reiterate our firm condemnation of the heinous terrorist attacks of 7 October and support the immediate release of all hostages, the text must decisively address the collapse of basic life-sustaining services in Gaza, particularly by guaranteeing the delivery of fuel to keep hospitals and critical infrastructure operational. We also stress the imperative of preventing any forced transfer of civilians and ensuring that humanitarian pauses are enacted without delay.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the initiative of the United States to bring forward a text aimed at addressing this grave crisis, but we must ensure the resolution reflects the urgent humanitarian imperatives on the ground. Building upon the broad agreement achieved around the Brazilian draft (S/2023/773), the text should explicitly call for the delivery of indispensable supplies—particularly fuel for hospitals—and address evacuation orders affecting civilians in northern Gaza. We urge all delegations to work collaboratively toward a balanced, consensus-driven outcome that protects all civilian lives and upholds international humanitarian law.
messages.Japan: Japan welcomes this draft, which unequivocally condemns the terror attacks by Hamas, calls for the immediate release of hostages, and addresses the critical need for humanitarian pauses. To ensure the Council can deliver tangible relief on the ground, we believe it is vital to explicitly reference the urgent facilitation of essential items such as fuel, as well as the protection of UN and humanitarian personnel. Japan strongly supports ongoing diplomatic efforts and stands ready to work with the penholder and all Council members toward adopting a united and actionable resolution.
messages.Malta: Malta welcomes the draft's clear condemnation of Hamas's terrorist acts, the call for the immediate release of hostages, and the inclusion of humanitarian pauses. However, to ensure the text genuinely meets the catastrophic humanitarian reality on the ground, we urge the inclusion of a clear call to rescind evacuation orders for northern Gaza and explicit reference to fuel supplies indispensable for hospital generators. As Chair of the Working Group on Children and Armed Conflict, Malta also stresses that the protection of children in Gaza must be explicitly addressed.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique appreciates the United States' initiative to seek Council action amid this catastrophic humanitarian crisis, where civilians, especially women and children, are bearing the brunt of the violence. To achieve the necessary unity and balance, the resolution must address the immediate realities on the ground, notably by calling for the rescission of the evacuation orders in northern Gaza and ensuring sustained humanitarian pauses that permit the entry of vital supplies, including fuel. The Security Council must act decisively to protect civilians, uphold international humanitarian law, and lay the groundwork for a political resolution.
messages.Russian Federation: The American draft is thoroughly one-sided, politicized, and completely detached from the reality on the ground. By deliberately avoiding a demand for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and asserting Article 51 self-defence, this text effectively provides cover and a green light for an impending ground operation and the ongoing collective punishment of the civilian population in Gaza. The Security Council cannot endorse such double standards; without a clear call for an immediate ceasefire and the rescinding of the unlawful evacuation order, this draft is unacceptable.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes the United States initiative and supports the draft's clear condemnation of Hamas's terror attacks and the call for the immediate release of hostages and humanitarian pauses. As depositary of the Geneva Conventions, we attach utmost importance to strict adherence to international humanitarian law by all parties. We urge the penholder to address the untenable evacuation order in northern Gaza and ensure explicit provision for essential fuel supplies to prevent the total collapse of life-saving services.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates cannot support the draft resolution in its current form, as it fundamentally fails to address the scale of the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. The Council must unequivocally call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, demand the revocation of the unviable evacuation orders for northern Gaza, and reject any attempt at forced displacement. Without these essential elements and a balanced approach that respects international humanitarian law and the rights of Palestinian civilians, this draft does not reflect the urgent demands of the Arab region or the international humanitarian community.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly welcomes this draft resolution, which rightly and unequivocally condemns Hamas's brutal terrorist attacks and explicitly affirms Israel's inherent right to self-defence in line with international humanitarian law. To ensure the Council fully reflects the realities on the ground, we urge the inclusion of explicit language condemning Hamas's abhorrent practice of using innocent civilians as human shields. We fully support the calls for humanitarian pauses and will work closely with the United States and Council partners to secure adoption.

Crucially, the text maintains essential US national security red lines: unequivocally condemning Hamas, demanding unconditional hostage releases, condemning human shields, and upholding the inherent right to self-defence under Article 51.

messages.Albania: Albania fully supports this draft resolution, which comprehensively reflects our core principles and priorities. The text rightly condemns Hamas's heinous terrorist attacks, demands the immediate release of all hostages, reaffirms the inherent right of self-defence under Article 51 of the Charter, and addresses urgent humanitarian needs in full compliance with international humanitarian law. We commend the United States for its diplomatic leadership and stand ready to vote in favour of the draft as presented.
messages.Brazil: Brazil cannot support the draft resolution in its current form, as it fails to incorporate the essential call for the rescission of the evacuation order for northern Gaza, an indispensable humanitarian provision that garnered overwhelming support in our draft resolution (S/2023/773). Furthermore, the unbalanced framing of self-defence in operative paragraph 2 lacks the necessary constraints under international humanitarian law and the principles of distinction and proportionality. Without these fundamental adjustments to protect civilian life and ensure adherence to international law, Brazil will be compelled to abstain.
messages.China: The current draft remains fundamentally unbalanced, evades the overwhelming call of the international community—especially Arab and Islamic countries—for an immediate ceasefire, and fails to demand the rescinding of the evacuation order and the lifting of the siege on Gaza. Furthermore, the draft's unbalanced language on self-defence risks giving a green light to continued military operations and the collective punishment of more than two million Gazans. If the penholder insists on putting a text to the vote that refuses to call for an immediate ceasefire and ignores the basic humanitarian imperatives on the ground, China will have no choice but to firmly oppose it.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador expresses its appreciation to the United States delegation for accommodating our concerns, particularly by incorporating the explicit reference to fuel in operative paragraph 3 and reinforcing protections against forced displacement and safeguards for civilians under operative paragraph 5. We believe this revised text strikes a necessary balance by unequivocally condemning the terrorist attacks by Hamas, reaffirming international humanitarian law, and demanding urgent, unhindered humanitarian access for civilians in Gaza. Ecuador stands ready to support this draft resolution when put to a vote.
messages.France: France thanks the United States for accommodating our key priorities, notably the inclusion of humanitarian corridors, the explicit mention of fuel and essential supplies, and the clear reaffirmation of international humanitarian law. The revised draft strikes an appropriate balance by condemning Hamas's heinous terrorist attacks, acknowledging Israel's right to defend itself in strict compliance with international humanitarian law, and addressing the dire humanitarian crisis in Gaza. France fully supports this draft resolution and is prepared to vote in favour.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the penholder's inclusion of essential supplies, specifically fuel, and strengthened safeguards against forced displacement in this revision. Our absolute priority is to overcome the Council's paralysis and ensure immediate, tangible relief for civilians facing an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. While we will support the draft to enable decisive Council action, we urge colleagues to reflect a clearer perspective toward silencing the guns.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the penholder's constructive efforts to accommodate key concerns, particularly regarding the urgent delivery of water, food, fuel, and medical supplies, as well as adherence to international humanitarian law. To ensure a balanced and effective text that truly protects vulnerable civilians, we continue to urge an explicit call for the rescission of the evacuation orders for northern Gaza. Ghana remains committed to Council unity and stands ready to support action that delivers immediate humanitarian relief and de-escalation.
messages.Japan: Japan appreciates the penholder's constructive engagement and the incorporation of our proposals regarding essential fuel supplies, humanitarian pauses, and the explicit protection of UNRWA personnel and facilities. The revised text strikes an appropriate balance by unequivocally condemning Hamas's terror attacks, reaffirming international humanitarian law, and addressing the dire humanitarian situation on the ground. Japan fully supports the draft resolution and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Malta: Malta welcomes the penholder's constructive engagement and the explicit incorporation of our priorities, particularly regarding fuel delivery, the protection of children under international humanitarian law, and safeguards against forced displacement. Given the catastrophic humanitarian reality reported by UN agencies and the WHO, we continue to urge Council members to explicitly call for the rescission of the northern Gaza evacuation order. With this inclusion, the draft presents a viable and balanced path forward for the Council to fulfill its responsibility to protect civilians.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique appreciates the inclusion of fuel and the reinforced references to international humanitarian law in the revised text. However, to adequately reflect the catastrophic realities on the ground, the resolution must clearly call for an immediate humanitarian pause and the rescission of evacuation orders affecting civilians in northern Gaza. Without a text that decisively halts the humanitarian collapse and fully safeguards civilian lives, the Council risks failing to meet its responsibilities.
messages.Russian Federation: The United States draft remains thoroughly unbalanced and unacceptable, serving solely to greenlight a devastating ground operation rather than halt the catastrophic bloodshed. By refusing to call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and attempting to misuse Article 51 of the UN Charter to grant carte blanche to an occupying power, the penholder renders this Council complicit in collective punishment. If these fundamental flaws are not rectified, the Russian Federation will vote against this text.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes the revised draft, which reflects our core priorities by incorporating explicit references to humanitarian pauses, essential supplies including fuel, and strict compliance by all parties with international humanitarian law, particularly the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution. While we maintain that evacuation orders affecting civilians must not lead to forced displacement and should ideally be rescinded, the strengthened protections in operative paragraph 5 provide vital safeguards. In the spirit of Council unity and urgency to address the humanitarian catastrophe and secure hostage releases, Switzerland supports this text and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates cannot support a text that fails to call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, which is urgently needed to halt the bloodshed and allow humanitarian operations to function. The draft remains fundamentally unbalanced by omitting an explicit demand for the rescission of the unlawful evacuation order for northern Gaza and failing to address the collective punishment of civilians in Gaza. If the Council cannot reflect these vital humanitarian imperatives and the unified position of the Arab Group, the UAE will vote against this resolution.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports this revised text, which addresses our core priorities. It rightly and unequivocally condemns Hamas's heinous terrorist attacks and its abhorrent use of human shields, affirms Israel's inherent right to self-defence under the UN Charter, and demands the immediate release of all hostages. At the same time, it emphasizes full compliance with international humanitarian law and the vital need for humanitarian pauses to get life-saving aid to civilians in Gaza.

steps.summary: The United States maintains the draft without amendment, standing firmly on its core foreign policy principles: unequivocally condemning Hamas's 7 October terrorist attacks, reaffirming Israel's inherent right to self-defence under Article 51, demanding the immediate release of hostages, and pursuing practical humanitarian pauses and aid delivery including fuel. The United States firmly rejects calls for an immediate ceasefire or the removal of self-defence language, which would only entrench Hamas's terror infrastructure and leave Israel vulnerable. The draft commands broad support from ten Council members, while Russia, China, and the UAE are expected to vote against it.

reasons.Albania: The draft resolution submitted by the United States explicitly condemns Hamas's terrorist attacks, demands the immediate release of hostages, and affirms Israel's inherent right to self-defence under Article 51, fully aligning with Albania's principled position and alliance commitments.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil abstains because its key concerns and amendments—notably regarding an explicit call to rescind the evacuation order for northern Gaza and a more balanced framing of international law obligations—were rejected by the penholder. As Council President, Brazil delivers its explanation of vote after the vote rather than before.
reasons.China: The United States draft resolution fails to reflect the international community's urgent call for an immediate ceasefire, evades the root causes of the conflict, and establishes a narrative that could justify further military escalation and the collective punishment of the civilian population in Gaza. As our core red lines regarding an immediate ceasefire, the lifting of the siege, and opposition to the forced displacement of civilians were completely rejected, China must cast a negative vote.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador supported the US draft resolution as it explicitly condemns Hamas terrorist acts, demands hostage releases, emphasizes strict adherence to international humanitarian law, and calls for humanitarian pauses to provide essential aid to civilians in Gaza. In line with Council practice, Ecuador will deliver its explanation of vote after the voting procedure concludes.
reasons.France: France supports the draft resolution as it condemns Hamas's terrorist attacks, reaffirms Israel's right to self-defence under international law, and addresses the critical humanitarian situation by calling for humanitarian pauses and full compliance with international humanitarian law.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon consistently prioritizes urgent Council action to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, condemn terrorism, and protect civilians, choosing to vote in favour of the text despite unaddressed amendment requests rather than contribute to continued Council paralysis.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana supports the draft resolution as it addresses urgent humanitarian concerns, demands the release of hostages, condemns terrorism, and upholds international humanitarian law and the two-State solution, despite its requested amendments regarding the evacuation order not being fully accommodated. In line with its diplomatic approach to achieve Council action and de-escalate the conflict, Ghana votes in favour.
reasons.Japan: Japan supports the draft resolution as it condemns Hamas's terrorist attacks, demands the immediate release of hostages, explicitly calls for humanitarian pauses and access including fuel, and aligns with Japan's close alliance with the United States and dedication to international humanitarian law.
reasons.Malta: Malta supports the draft resolution as it explicitly condemns Hamas's terrorist acts, demands the unconditional release of hostages, reaffirms international humanitarian law, and calls for urgent humanitarian pauses and corridors to alleviate the catastrophic suffering of civilians in Gaza. Although our specific request regarding the formal rescission of the evacuation order was not fully incorporated, the text's strong provisions on humanitarian access and the protection of civilians warrant an affirmative vote.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique abstains because the draft resolution fails to incorporate crucial amendments calling for the rescission of the evacuation order in northern Gaza and falls short of demanding an immediate, sustained humanitarian ceasefire necessary to address the catastrophic humanitarian emergency.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft resolution fails to call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and instead legitimizes Israel's military operation and potential ground invasion under Article 51, violating Russia's fundamental red lines. Consequently, Russia exercises its veto against the US-sponsored text while continuing to advocate for its own balanced ceasefire draft.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the US-led draft resolution because it clearly condemns Hamas's terrorist attacks, calls for the immediate and unconditional release of hostages, demands strict respect for international humanitarian law, and calls for humanitarian pauses to ensure unhindered aid delivery, including fuel, to civilians in Gaza.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The UAE votes against the draft resolution because the penholder rejected its red-line requests, notably the demand for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the rescission of evacuation orders in northern Gaza, and addressing the collective punishment of Gazan civilians.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft resolution unequivocally condemns Hamas's terrorist atrocities, recognizes Israel's inherent right to self-defence under Article 51, and addresses the critical need for humanitarian pauses and civilian protection, aligning directly with the UK's core positions and close alliance with the United States.
reasons.United States of America: As the penholder and sponsor of this draft resolution, the United States votes in favour of its own text, which reflects key US foreign policy priorities including explicitly condemning Hamas, recognizing Israel's right to self-defence, and calling for humanitarian pauses.

before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation cannot support the draft resolution submitted by the United States. 

The document before us is deeply politicized and thoroughly unbalanced. Most crucially, it lacks the single most vital element demanded by the entire international community and the catastrophic situation on the ground: an immediate, unconditional, and durable humanitarian ceasefire. Without a ceasefire, any talk of humanitarian access or "pauses" is completely meaningless, as aid cannot be delivered safely while bombs continue to rain down on residential neighborhoods, schools, and hospitals in the Gaza Strip.

Furthermore, this text is clearly designed not to save civilians, but to provide political cover and a green light for an impending Israeli ground offensive in Gaza under the guise of an unlimited right to self-defence. An occupying Power cannot invoke the right to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter, as confirmed by the International Court of Justice in its 2004 Advisory Opinion. 

The American draft also ignores the root causes of the conflict, fails to demand the rescission of the unlawful evacuation order forced upon more than a million Palestinians in northern Gaza, and refuses to condemn the indiscriminate strikes that have already cost thousands of innocent Palestinian lives, including thousands of children. 

The Security Council must not become an instrument for advancing the geopolitical ambitions of Washington and its allies at the expense of human lives in the Middle East. For these reasons, Russia will vote against this draft resolution.
before.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The United Arab Emirates will vote against the draft resolution submitted by the United States. 

Over the past two weeks, the catastrophic situation in the Gaza Strip has worsened exponentially. More than 5,000 Palestinians, including thousands of children, have been killed, and civilian infrastructure has been decimated. The United Nations and humanitarian agencies have repeatedly told us that Gaza is running out of time, water, food, fuel, and life itself. 

Yet, this draft resolution fails to call for what is most urgently needed on the ground: an immediate, durable, and fully respected humanitarian ceasefire. It does not call for the rescission of the evacuation orders forcing over a million Palestinians to flee their homes with nowhere safe to go, nor does it firmly reject forced displacement. Furthermore, the draft does not adequately recognize that the principles of international humanitarian law must apply equally and without exception, and that the right of self-defence can never justify the collective punishment of an entire civilian population under siege.

Every hour that this Council fails to demand a ceasefire, more innocent lives are lost. As the Arab member on this Council, we cannot endorse a text that overlooks these essential humanitarian imperatives and the overwhelming consensus of our region. For these reasons, the UAE will cast a negative vote.

Thank you.
before.United States of America:
Colleagues, since the horrific terrorist attacks of October 7, the United States has been actively engaged in intensive diplomacy on the ground to address this crisis. Today, we have put forward a resolution that reflects those diplomatic realities and addresses the fundamental issues before this Council.

First and foremost, this draft resolution unequivocally condemns the heinous terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. It explicitly reaffirms the inherent right of all States to individual and collective self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter—a foundational principle that this Council has recognized time and again after terrorist atrocities. 

At the same time, this text clearly underscores that all parties must comply with international humanitarian law and that civilian lives must be protected. It calls for practical measures, including humanitarian pauses, to allow lifesaving aid—food, water, medicine, and fuel—to safely reach civilians in Gaza. It supports the vital work being carried out by the United Nations and regional partners, and it warns against any regional spillover that would plunge the Middle East into a wider conflict.

The United States has engaged extensively and incorporated feedback from all Council members to build a strong, balanced, and actionable text. It is time for this Council to speak with one voice, condemn terrorism, support the protection of civilians, and advance humanitarian relief. We urge all members of the Security Council to vote in favour of this resolution.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United States. 

We did so because this text finally addressed the core issues that this Council has struggled to articulate since the horrific events of 7 October. It did what was right and necessary: it unequivocally condemned the barbarous and monstrous terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas against Israel; it demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; and, crucially, it explicitly reaffirmed the inherent right of Israel, as of any sovereign State, to self-defence under Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations. As we have stated before in this chamber, no nation faced with such terror could be denied that fundamental right.

At the same time, the draft resolution rightly and clearly placed paramount importance on the protection of civilians, the strict adherence by all parties to international humanitarian law, and the urgent need to address the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. It called for actionable measures, including humanitarian pauses and corridors, to allow life-saving aid—food, water, medicine, and fuel—to reach civilians in desperate need, while upholding the principle that civilians must never be targets or used as human shields. 

It is therefore deeply regrettable that, despite receiving the support of a clear majority of the Council, this balanced and practical text was blocked by the veto. Once again, narrow political calculations have prevented the Security Council from discharging its primary responsibility to uphold international peace and security and to respond effectively to a grave humanitarian crisis.

Albania remains convinced that terrorism must be confronted and defeated, that civilians must be protected without distinction, and that the only viable path to lasting peace, security, and dignity for both Israelis and Palestinians lies in the realization of the two-State solution.

I thank you.
after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil abstained on the draft resolution presented by the United States.

Just one week ago, this Council had before it a draft resolution—presented by Brazil after extensive consultations and broad compromise—that gathered the support of 12 members of this Council and reflected a delicate, carefully negotiated balance. That text unequivocally condemned the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas, demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, called for humanitarian pauses to allow life-saving aid into Gaza, and urged the rescission of the evacuation order for northern Gaza, strictly adhering to international humanitarian law. Unfortunately, that draft was vetoed.

While we recognize the efforts made by the United States in presenting this text and acknowledge the inclusion of important elements, including the condemnation of terrorism and the call for humanitarian access and pauses, the draft resolution before us today failed to achieve the necessary balance to unite this Council and respond effectively to the unfolding catastrophe. 

In particular, the text did not adequately address the full scale of the humanitarian emergency on the ground. It fell short of clearly addressing the evacuation orders affecting over one million civilians in Gaza, who have nowhere safe to go, and it did not place sufficient emphasis on the urgent, imperative need to halt the hostilities to protect civilians and avert a wider regional conflagration.

The situation in Gaza is catastrophic. Thousands of civilians, predominantly women and children, have been killed, critical civilian infrastructure and hospitals have collapsed, and essential supplies—food, water, electricity, and fuel—have been depleted. International humanitarian law is not optional; its principles of distinction, precaution, and proportionality must be respected by all parties at all times. Collective punishment cannot be accepted under any circumstances.

Brazil deeply regrets that once again, division and national interests have prevented the Security Council from fulfilling its primary responsibility under the Charter for the maintenance of international peace and security. Our inaction costs human lives with every passing hour. We must redouble our collective efforts to find common ground, ensure immediate and unhindered humanitarian relief, protect all civilians, and revive the prospect of a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution.

Thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted against the draft resolution submitted by the United States. 

Our position is based on facts, on law, on conscience, on justice, and on the overwhelming appeal of the international community, especially Arab countries.

Last week, when a draft resolution focused on the humanitarian situation and calling for humanitarian pauses was put to the vote, the United States exercised its veto, which left the Council in shock and widespread disappointment. Last Saturday evening, the United States circulated a new draft resolution. This draft departs from the spirit of previous Council resolutions and integrates many elements that remain deeply divisive, going far beyond the humanitarian sphere. Most crucially, the draft resolution evades the most urgent issue: calling for an immediate and durable ceasefire.

A ceasefire is not just a diplomatic phrase; it is a matter of life and death for countless innocent civilians in Gaza. If a Security Council resolution fails to issue an unequivocal and strong call for an immediate ceasefire, it is equivalent to providing tacit consent and giving a green light to further military escalation and civilian catastrophe. Such an outcome is completely unacceptable.

Furthermore, the draft resolution fails to reflect the root causes of the current conflict and attempts to establish a new narrative on the Palestinian question. It ignores the prolonged occupation of Palestinian territories and evades the legitimate rights and aspirations of the Palestinian people. The draft is gravely unbalanced and blurs the lines between self-defence and violations of international humanitarian law. It does not call for the immediate rescission of the evacuation order for northern Gaza, nor does it strongly condemn the collective punishment imposed on the people of Gaza.

China does not oppose the Council taking action; on the contrary, we have always strongly supported the Council in playing a responsible role. However, the action taken by the Council must stand the test of history, conscience, and international law. We must never adopt a resolution that would lead to further escalation of violence and plunge the region into an even deeper abyss. 

China will continue to stand firmly on the side of peace, justice, and international law. We call on all members of the Council to heed the strong voice of the international community, place the lives of innocent civilians above all else, genuinely commit to a ceasefire, stop the hostilities, open humanitarian corridors, and work tirelessly toward a comprehensive, just, and lasting solution to the question of Palestine.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United States. 

We deeply regret that the Security Council was once again unable to unite and take action today, due to the vetoes cast by two permanent members.

The text submitted by the United States contained essential elements that this Council should have endorsed without hesitation. First, it unequivocally condemned the heinous terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas and other terrorist groups against Israel on 7 October, as well as the taking of hostages, and demanded their immediate and unconditional release. Nothing can ever justify such acts of terror. 

Second, the text reaffirmed the right of all States to self-defence in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, while recalling an essential principle: that all parties must scrupulously respect international humanitarian law in all circumstances, including the principles of distinction, precaution, and proportionality, and ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure.

Third, the text responded to the catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip. It called for urgent humanitarian pauses and corridors to allow full, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access, so that essential supplies—water, electricity, food, medicine, and fuel—can reach civilian populations in dire need. 

In the face of this tragedy, the Security Council cannot remain silent and paralyzed. The protection of all civilian lives, whether Israeli or Palestinian, is an absolute moral and legal imperative. A humanitarian truce is urgently needed to allow assistance to reach civilians and to facilitate the release of hostages, and this truce could lead to a sustainable ceasefire.

Finally, we must not lose sight of the political horizon. Only the two-State solution, with two democratic States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders, will bring just and lasting peace and stability to the region. France will continue to spare no effort to ensure that the Council shoulders its responsibilities.

Thank you.
after.Switzerland:
Switzerland voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United States. 

Since 7 October, Switzerland has firmly condemned the heinous acts of terror, indiscriminate attacks, and taking of hostages carried out by Hamas against the Israeli population. We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Switzerland recognizes Israel's legitimate right to ensure its defence and security in accordance with Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations. At the same time, we recall that all parties are strictly bound to comply with international law, in particular international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution in the conduct of hostilities must be scrupulously respected, and civilians and civilian objects—including schools, hospitals, and United Nations facilities—must be protected under all circumstances.

Switzerland remains deeply alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian situation unfolding in the Gaza Strip. The civilian population is in desperate need of water, electricity, food, medical supplies, and fuel. Rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access throughout the Gaza Strip must be urgently guaranteed, and measures such as humanitarian pauses and corridors must be implemented to facilitate the delivery of life-saving relief.

The draft resolution presented by the United States reflected several of these vital elements, including the condemnation of terror, the call for the release of hostages, the obligation of all parties to respect international humanitarian law, the urgent need for humanitarian pauses and access, and the reaffirmed commitment to a two-State solution. For these reasons, Switzerland supported the draft text.

We deeply regret that the Council has once again failed to overcome its divisions and adopt a resolution at a moment of such acute crisis. In the face of immense human suffering and the real risk of a wider regional conflagration, it remains the duty of this Council to act unitedly to protect civilians and uphold international peace and security.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr. President,

The United Kingdom is deeply disappointed that the Security Council was once again unable to agree on a resolution and take decisive action in response to this crisis, following the vetoes cast by the Russian Federation and China. 

The United Kingdom voted in favour of the draft resolution tabled by the United States because it directly addressed the vital elements necessary to respond to the catastrophic events unfolding on the ground. 

First, the draft resolution rightly and unequivocally condemned the abhorrent, barbaric terrorist attacks committed by Hamas on 7 October—the largest loss of Jewish life in a single day since the Holocaust. It demanded the immediate, unconditional, and safe release of all hostages held in Gaza and condemned the cowardly use of civilians as human shields. 

Second, the text clearly reaffirmed the inherent right of all States to self-defence in line with Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations. As my Prime Minister has made clear, the United Kingdom stands with Israel and supports its right to defend itself against terrorism, deter further attacks, and secure its long-term safety. 

Third, the draft resolution addressed the desperate humanitarian situation facing civilians in Gaza. It called for all necessary measures, including humanitarian pauses and corridors, to enable the rapid, safe, and unhindered delivery of lifesaving humanitarian assistance—water, food, medicine, and fuel—to civilians in dire need. 

Crucially, the resolution underscored that all actions must be conducted in strict accordance with international humanitarian law, emphasizing the protection of civilians and critical civilian infrastructure, including United Nations facilities, hospitals, and humanitarian personnel. It also called on all actors to prevent a regional escalation of the conflict and reaffirmed our shared commitment to a negotiated two-State solution.

This was a serious, substantive draft that reflected intensive diplomatic efforts to address both the security and humanitarian imperatives of this crisis. It is profoundly regrettable that members of this Council chose to block it. 

The United Kingdom will continue to work tirelessly with our international partners to secure the release of all hostages, ensure the scaling-up of essential humanitarian aid to Gaza, protect civilians, and prevent regional contagion.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.United States of America:
Although today’s vote was a setback, make no mistake: we are not deterred. The United States will continue to do the hard work of diplomacy on the ground to secure the release of hostages, surge humanitarian assistance to civilians in Gaza, and prevent the conflict from spreading. 

We are deeply disappointed that Russia and China chose to veto this resolution. The United States put forward a serious, balanced, and constructive text. We engaged in extensive, transparent consultations and incorporated feedback and proposals from nearly every member of this Council. Our draft affirmed the right of all States to self-defence in accordance with the UN Charter, called for humanitarian pauses to get life-saving aid to civilians in Gaza, demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas, and underscored the imperative of protecting civilian lives and adhering to international humanitarian law.

Yet, Russia and China decided to veto it. Let us be clear: Russia and China did not veto this text because it was unbalanced; they vetoed it for cynical political reasons. They simply did not want to see a resolution put forward by the United States succeed, regardless of the message it sent to the world or the aid it sought to deliver to innocent civilians suffering in Gaza. Russia, in particular, continues to act in bad faith, showing that it is far more interested in scoring cheap geopolitical points than in advancing peace or addressing the urgent humanitarian catastrophe on the ground.

A majority of Council members voted in favour of this text today because it met the moment and addressed the critical realities on the ground. Despite this obstruction, the United States will not walk away from our responsibility. We will continue working tirelessly with our partners in the region and around the world to save lives, protect civilians, secure the release of hostages, and lay the foundation for a durable peace based on a two-State solution.
